People often ask me if I enjoy detaining ships. I have detained eleven ships in nine years, and I did not enjoy it once. My decision is very narrow. I record what I find. If the lifeboat gear was not serviced, that is a deficiency, and it goes on the record. The master can agree or not. But I do not decide if it matters. The rules require that every deficiency be recorded against the ship. Detention is a different decision. A person in an office, who never saw the ship, reviews it. That is not a weakness. It is the design of the system.
